newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus nationalist protest erupts in clashes.
newsitem.headline: Belarus nationalist protest erupts in clashes.

text.p: Nationalists battled with police in Belarus on Sunday as a protest against President Alexander Lukashenko's pro-Moscow policies erupted in clashes.
Police beat protesters with truncheons and nationalists fought back with their fists after about 4,000 demonstrators ignored a ban on marching.
Fighting also broke out at a sanctioned rally on Yakob Kolas Square, where a crowd of about 10,000 protesters had gathered.
A Reuters correspondent on the square said some protesters appeared to have been injured.

Protesters at the unsanctioned march attacked several police cars, shouting "Belarus into NATO" and "We will not sell our nation's glory" to express their hatred for Lukashenko's policy of forming a union with neighbouring Russia.
The nationalists, waving red and white nationalist flags which Lukashenko has replaced with Soviet emblems, were marking the anniversary of an independent republic created in 1918.
The republic lasted only a few months until it was incorporated by Russian Bolsheviks and Belarus stayed under Moscow rule until the Soviet Union collapsed in 1991.
Unlike people in other former Soviet republics, the majority of the population of 10 million favours closer ties with Moscow.

Sunday's was the latest in a string of protests against Lukashenko, who has cracked down on opposition forces by restricting rallies, arresting protesters and putting a senior opposition leader in prison in recent weeks.
A loose union of prominent politicians, nationalists, intellectuals and students mostly in the capital oppose Lukashenko, who was awarded sweeping powers in a landslide referendum win last November.
Western officials said the vote was illegitimate because Lukashenko ignored the old constitution to push it through.

The United States, one of the most vociferous foreign critics of the former farm chief's increasingly authoritarian rule, said two days ago that it had cut off $40 million in aid to Belarus because of its human rights performance.
